bull_bear.body: Conservative balance sheet (net debt/equity 0.6x); cash flow constrained by strategic inventory buildup (raw materials, camphor); no dividend or buyback mentioned; prioritizing margin recovery over shareholder returns
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Persistent Chinese dumping in aroma ingredients; oversupply in Indian camphor market; prolonged Mahad ramp-up delays; margin compression if pricing doesn't recover; inventory liquidity risk
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on volume growth and long-term margin recovery; transparent about short-term pain from Mahad and pricing; dismissive of anti-dumping petition for camphor; focused on operational efficiency and customer retention
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Mahad plant is EBITDA negative now but product is already being sold; hydrogenation plant is EBITDA positive and integrated; camphor imports are natural (not synthetic), so not direct competition; trading division is growing but not segmented in reporting
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Net Debt-to-Equity Ratio improved to 0.56x as of June 30, 2026, reflecting the Company's continued focus on disciplined capital allocation, prudent financial management and strengthening its balance sheet."
- Deck's Net D/E (x) chart shows 0.30 (FY24), 0.51 (FY25), 0.58 (FY26) — i.e. the June-2026 0.56x is an improvement off the FY26 level.
- The deck discloses no dividend policy, buyback, or reinvestment framework.

business.body:
- "One of the largest Indian manufacturers of a variety of Aroma Chemicals, Camphor, Fragrances and Flavours" and "one of the privileged few integrated manufacturers of fragrances and flavours as well as aroma chemicals globally".
- Stated aspiration: "to become a global player in the specialty aroma chemicals and use these synergies to become one of the most prominent fragrance and flavour companies"; the deck calls the company "a one stop solution provider for the flavour and fragrance industry".
- Lineage: the Fragrance and Flavours business was founded by Mr. Keshavlal Bodani in 1955 and has been "nurtured and handed down to three generations of the Bodani's".
- FY26 geographical sales split (deck chart): Domestic 67%, International 33%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Corporate history] In August 2008 Oriental Aromatics Ltd. acquired a controlling stake of 57.66% in the listed entity Camphor & Allied Products Ltd. (CAPL); in April 2017 Oriental Aromatics was fully amalgamated into the listed entity and CAPL was renamed Oriental Aromatics Limited.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoter 74.17%, Public 25.83%.
- [Investor relations] Investor relations is handled by an external agency, Valorem Advisors, which carries its own disclaimer in the deck.

deepdive.thesis: Record sales volume growth (30% QoQ) driven by market share gains, but EBITDA margin collapsed to 6.34% due to pricing pressure from Chinese dumping and Mahad plant ramp-up drag; margins expected to recover as Mahad reaches 60%+ utilization and cost optimization matures.

open.item: The Mahad greenfield facility has completed sampling cycles, commenced commercial shipments and qualified to participate in major global RFQs for the second half of 2026.
Accelerate the commercial ramp-up of the Mahad greenfield specialty aroma ingredients facility in FY 2026-27.
Drive volume growth, strengthen market position and progressively improve margins through internal efficiency and process improvement initiatives in FY 2026-27.
The Company states it is committed to expanding the global reach of its generic aroma ingredients while continuing to deliver value to customers worldwide.
OAL states it is moving its long-term strategic investments from the phase of capacity creation into commercial execution.
Immediate focus is on consolidating the manufacturing investments already made and maximising the potential of existing assets, remaining open to but not prioritising future expansion.
The Mahad facility currently has an estimated 1% to 1.5% impact on consolidated EBITDA margins during its ramp-up phase.
Management stated the Ambernath flavour and fragrance plant operates at one shift, with the ability to expand capacity by adding shifts.

Continue to expand the retail B2C footprint of the internalised heritage camphor brands Saraswati and 3 Pine to improve brand-led participation and reduce exposure to bulk B2B camphor pricing pressure.

Its integration from complex chemistry and molecule synthesis through to formulation positions it as a long-term supply partner to national and international FMCG, pharmaceutical and perfumery brands. The Company sells into more than 35 countries across five continents and also owns retail camphor brands serving India's spiritual and household markets.

risks.note: Global aroma ingredient markets remained buyer-led, limiting pricing power and keeping end-product realisations subdued; in a buyers' market, customer resistance to price increases can delay full recovery of raw material cost inflation.
risks.risk: Buyer's market and limited pricing power in aroma ingredients

risks.note: Capacities built by Chinese players continued to flow into non-tariff markets including India, Southeast Asia and parts of Europe, creating intense pricing pressure. OAL responded by prioritising volume leadership, market share and customer retention over short-term margins and by running a CPR (process re-engineering) programme to structurally reduce costs.
risks.risk: Chinese capacity pressure and dumping in non-tariff markets

risks.note: The Indian camphor market remained impacted by supply exceeding demand due to substantial domestic capacity additions, and natural camphor imports from China continued to influence pricing; exposure to highly competitive B2B commodity camphor meant low pricing power and margin compression. OAL internalised its heritage brands (Saraswati, 3 Pine, Bhimseni), shifting 60% of the camphor business into the formulated B2C space.
risks.risk: Domestic camphor overcapacity and product concentration in commodity B2B camphor

risks.note: Gum turpentine, crude sulphate turpentine and alpha-pinene prices remained elevated while crude-based raw materials were volatile and difficult to source; Rupee depreciation affected the imported portion of the raw material basket across all three divisions. OAL secured feedstock ahead of festive production cycles and held higher inventory when prices were perceived to be lowest.
risks.risk: Input cost inflation and currency depreciation

risks.note: Uncertainty over North American tariffs (which briefly reached 50% for certain categories) and global trade instability impacted export volumes and inventory building by U.S. customers; OAL evaluated alternate market channels and, following a new trade deal, is leveraging a restored 20% tariff advantage over Chinese competitors.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and trade risk / tariff exposure of the export book

risks.note: Early-stage ramp-up of the Mahad facility, alongside soft aroma ingredient pricing and buyer-market conditions, weighed on profitability; management's priority is to stabilise Mahad and accelerate its commercial ramp-up.
risks.risk: Execution and margin drag from the Mahad greenfield ramp-up

risks.note: Rapid asset creation and debt-funded expansion could strain the balance sheet during a soft pricing environment; OAL states it followed a conservative capital structure with net debt-to-equity kept at 0.60x to 0.65x.
risks.risk: Financial leverage from rapid, debt-funded asset creation

risks.note: Significant demand fluctuations between quarters (Q1 and Q3 traditionally softer than the festive peak in Q2) can create revenue and cash-flow volatility, while broader macroeconomic uncertainty led to cautious consumer behaviour with fragrances and flavours still perceived at the margin as discretionary. A diversified mix across fragrances, aroma ingredients and camphor is the stated cushion.
risks.risk: Seasonality and cautious discretionary consumer demand
